claim_boundary: Minimized deterministic state derived from the exported live run; it is not a claim that the original task completed.

run_identity_defect.note: The target workspace was named neon-serpents-cli-002 (leftover from an earlier, unrelated slice) but the submitted goal was a Pixel Wanderer local browser game. The workspace folder name is not mission authority, but the operator had no on-screen signal of the real goal/contract before the run got stuck, which is why RUN_045 PART H adds a Run Identity panel driven only by the raw goal / Mission Contract, never the workspace label.

repair_that_executed.note: A targeted static-repair instruction was written, the callable backend ran it, the response was ingested, and the repair write executed (added the missing R-key restart handler). This is the same repair shape as the cli_011 fixture -- the defect is not in the repair itself.

root_cause.description: Once a callable-backend response had been consumed and no retry/reinvoke was pending, the branch unconditionally returned HA_NEXT_NONE. It never checked whether repair_phase had just finished a post-write phase (repair_executing/repair_verifying) that requires scheduling a static or runtime re-verification. The pre-existing repair_phase check further down in the function could never run because the callable-backend fallback already returned first.
root_cause.class: general state-machine/liveness defect in the post-repair transition, not specific to Pixel Wanderer, game controls, or the browser runtime

state_invariant_violation.message: mode=waiting_for_agent persisted with no legitimate pending backend/runtime/human condition.
